name: Meta Kuna Data Center
summary: Meta data center in Kuna, Idaho, about 16 miles from downtown Boise. Announced in February 2022 as a USD 800 million campus with more than 960,000 sq ft of data center space expected by 2025, it broke ground in 2022 and was later paused for a redesign to support AI infrastructure and liquid cooling. Meta began serving traffic from it in the third quarter of 2026, citing a USD 1.2 billion investment and a facility of more than 750,000 sq ft. Meta says it planned its energy needs with Idaho Power, and it built a water and wastewater system that it handed to the City of Kuna.

location.note: Coordinates are the Kuna city coordinates from its Wikipedia page. Sources name the city and county but give no address or parcel.

notes: Reported sizes differ: more than 960,000 sq ft in the 2022 plan versus more than 750,000 sq ft for the finished facility in 2026. Meta's water and wastewater commitment was reported as about USD 50 million in 2022; Meta's 2026 fact sheet puts it at more than USD 100 million. The fact sheet (s1) shows no publication date (embedded file creation date 2026-09-02), so figures that rest on it alone are dated to the access date, 2026-10-09. Meta's investment figures are framed as investment in Idaho; Baxtel's report ties the USD 1.2 billion to the Kuna campus.

parties.name: Idaho Power
parties.note: State regulators expect the data center to become Idaho Power's single largest customer.

parties.name: City of Kuna
parties.note: Owns and operates the water and wastewater treatment system that Meta built and handed over.

milestones.note: Reported in early September 2026 as open and serving traffic, after a construction pause for redesign; in 2022 the campus had been expected by 2025.

power_sources.description: Idaho Power serves the site; at announcement Meta said the campus would be supported by renewable energy through Idaho Power's Clean Energy Your Way program, and Meta says it pays the full cost of the energy it uses.
